newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr top seen limited, confined to ranges.
newsitem.headline: Dlr top seen limited, confined to ranges.

text.p: The dollar is likely to be top-heavy against the yen and the mark in Asia on Friday, with trading seen confined to narrow ranges ahead of U.S. inflation data later today, dealers said.

The dollar may attempt to break through a key support at 111.00 yen, but heavy bids from Japanese investors including a Japanese public fund expected at 110.90-111.00 yen could prevent the dollar from falling much, dealers said.
"The dollar will stay top-heavy, carrying over a trend from earlier this week," said a trust bank dealer. "But the downside will be also limited," he added.
Earlier this week, the dollar fell as low as around 111.00 yen in New York but faced extremely strong bids there, making traders reluctant to take large sell positions.

Another bank dealer said heavy buying interest from Japanese investors such as life insurers was expected at 110.80-111.00 yen and this could deter the dollar from tumbling even if it temporarily dips below 111 yen.
Stop-loss dollar sales are expected to take place at 110.80-85 yen, said the trust bank dealer.
"The key would be how U.S. financial markets perform in reaction to today's U.S. inflation data, " he added.
September U.S. wholesale prices and retail sales will be released at 1230 GMT.

Economists polled by Reuters estimate that the Producer Price Index (PPI) rose 0.3 percent in September and increased 0.2 percent when the more volatile food and energy items in the index were set aside.

Larger-than-expected figures could rattle the U.S. stock and bond markets, which could also hurt the dollar, said the trust bank dealer. "Over the past month or so, the dollar's strength has been supported by the well-performing U.S. stock and bond markets," he added.
